claims.text: Overall Green Flood in Afghanistan from 19 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC to 21 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC. Flood can have a low humanitarian impact based on the magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability. At least 20 people were killed, around 80 others injured, and more than 100 remain missing, in Nuristan Province following flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: the ReliefWeb disaster page's Latest Updates list shows an IFRC DREF Operation report (MDRAF022, posted 6 August 2026) as the newest item; no OCHA Flash Update #4 or newer WHO situation report has been published. The IFRC report documents damage specifically in Parun City (30 houses damaged, of which 7 destroyed; destruction of a mosque, the municipality building, and seven markets; roughly 45 livestock lost) without providing an updated aggregate death toll. The combined confirmed toll (at least 30 deaths) is unchanged.

ReliefWeb's disaster record (FF-2026-000120-AFG) still shows Status: Ongoing; the latest posted item remains UNICEF's Flash Update No. 3 (originally published 11 Aug 2026, posted 13 Aug 2026) confirming a second flash flood struck Barg-e-Matal district, Nuristan, on 3 August, affecting 191 families. No newer update has been posted as of this check.

UN News (22 July 2026): flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall on 20 July have killed at least 26 people across eastern Afghanistan, including 23 in Nuristan province, where homes, markets and roads were swept away, with the worst devastation in Parun City (7 houses completely destroyed, 23 partially damaged, 70 shops and 11 hotels damaged, 40 vehicles lost). The floods also killed three Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing with Pakistan and injured nine others there. OCHA said the immediate priority is to save lives and reach people who may still be missing or injured, and warned that casualty figures could rise as more information becomes available; UNICEF and partners are setting up a field clinic in Parun for trauma care.

OCHA Flash Update #2: Flooding in Eastern Afghanistan (22-23 July 2026): in Parun City, Nuristan Province, local authorities report 23 killed, 5 missing (down from over 100) and 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor). At the Torkham transit camp in Nangarhar, 3 Afghan refugees were killed and 9 injured (unchanged). One additional death is reported in Maidan Wardak province (Sayedabad District). The response has moved from immediate search and rescue and emergency life-saving assistance towards a broader, multi-sector response addressing shelter, health, food, WASH, protection, livelihoods and planning to address early recovery needs.

OCHA Flash Update #3: Flooding in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Afghanistan (as of 28 July 2026): in Laghman Province, three people were killed and four others injured, with 187 families affected and 183 houses damaged or destroyed; approximately 800 acres of seasonal crops and around 310 livestock were also reportedly lost or damaged. Nuristan Province remains the most severely affected area; the completed inter-agency needs assessment in Parun district identified 120 families eligible for humanitarian assistance, of which the first 92 have already received assistance. The Shelter/NFI cluster reports 1,168 families have been affected across 14 provinces, including 234 houses completely destroyed and 930 houses damaged. Needs assessments in Maidan Wardak and Panjshir are expected to commence shortly.

WHO's Situation Report No. 3 on the flash floods in Afghanistan (published 3 August 2026 on ReliefWeb, data as of 15:00 on 30 July 2026, described by WHO as its final situation report on this response) records cumulative Key Figures of 29 fatalities, 129 injuries and 4 missing, broken down as 26 deaths in the Eastern region (23 Nuristan, 3 Laghman), 1 death in the Central region, and further deaths in Paktika's Barmal district and Paktia province in the Southeastern region. This WHO cumulative figure reflects domestic flood-affected provinces only and does not include the 3 Afghan refugees killed at the Torkham border transit camp that OCHA's Flash Update series counted toward the combined 30-death toll already on file; the two figures use different scopes and neither supersedes the other.

published.description: Flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall struck Afghanistan's eastern Nuristan Province around 19 July 2026, devastating the provincial capital Parun and its surrounding villages, and also killed Afghan refugees at a returnee transit camp near the Torkham border crossing; GDACS assessed the initial flood at a Green alert level. OCHA's Flash Update series records 23 killed in Parun City with 125 injured and 5 missing, plus deaths at Torkham, in Maidan Wardak and in Laghman Province, for a combined confirmed toll of at least 30 deaths across central, eastern and southeastern Afghanistan; the Shelter/NFI cluster counts 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces, with 234 houses destroyed and 930 damaged. WHO closed its reporting with a final situation report (3 August 2026) recording 29 fatalities and 129 injuries on its narrower domestic scope. A second flash flood struck Barg-e-Matal district in Nuristan on 3 August, affecting 191 families; the response remains ongoing.

impact.summary: The combined confirmed death toll is at least 30: 23 killed in Parun City (125 injured, 5 missing), 3 Afghan refugees killed at the Torkham transit camp, 1 death in Maidan Wardak and 3 in Laghman Province, where 187 families were affected. The Shelter/NFI cluster reports 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces (234 houses destroyed, 930 damaged); WHO's final situation report records 29 fatalities and 129 injuries on its domestic-only scope, and a second flash flood hit Barg-e-Matal district on 3 August, affecting 191 families.

location.region: Nuristan Province (Parun and surrounding villages), with additional flood impacts confirmed in Laghman, Ghazni, Kapisa, Logar, Nangarhar, Paktia, Paktika and Parwan provinces

updates.text: UNICEF's Flash Update No. 3, posted to ReliefWeb, confirmed that a second flash flood struck Barg-e-Matal district, Nuristan, on 3 August, affecting 191 families; ReliefWeb's disaster record for the floods remains listed as ongoing.

An IFRC DREF operation report documented flood damage in Parun City: 30 houses damaged, of which 7 were destroyed; a mosque, the municipality building and seven markets destroyed; and roughly 45 livestock lost. It provided no updated aggregate death toll.

WHO issued its final situation report on the response (No. 3, data as of 30 July), recording a cumulative 29 fatalities, 129 injuries and 4 missing across the Eastern, Central and Southeastern regions — a domestic scope that excludes the 3 refugees killed at the Torkham transit camp.

OCHA's Flash Update #3 broadened reporting to central, eastern and southeastern Afghanistan: 3 people were killed and 4 injured in Laghman Province, with 187 families affected and 183 houses damaged or destroyed, bringing the combined confirmed toll to at least 30 deaths. The Shelter/NFI cluster counted 1,168 families affected across 14 provinces.

OCHA's Flash Update #2 revised the Parun City toll to 23 killed, 125 injured (38 severe, 87 minor) and 5 missing — down from more than 100 initially feared missing; 3 Afghan refugees killed at the Torkham transit camp and 1 death in Maidan Wardak's Sayedabad District were unchanged.

claims.text: GDACS's event report for a Green-alert forest fire in Algeria (18-22 July 2026 window, Seraidi/Constantine area) cites about 11,362 hectares burned and roughly 2,870 people exposed. Algeria's interior ministry reported six deaths from the wildfires, and authorities reported more than 100 people hospitalised in the town of Seraidi and about 150 homes damaged there.

GDACS's event report for a second concurrent Green-alert forest fire in Algeria, now at episode 6 covering an 18-24 July 2026 window, cites about 14,082 hectares burned. Algeria's interior ministry registered six deaths in relation to the fires affecting multiple provinces during this period; four people were arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting fires.

GDACS's event report for a third concurrent Green-alert forest fire in Algeria, now at episode 5 covering a 21-24 July 2026 window, cites about 13,388 hectares burned, assessed as low humanitarian impact based on burned area and affected population. Thermal-anomaly detections continue to be recorded as of 24 July 2026.

Over the last 24 hours, the Ministry of the Interior, Local Authorities and Transport confirmed six fatalities linked to the wildfires. In Seraïdi, Annaba, more than 100 patients were evacuated from a rehabilitation hospital, while approximately 150 homes were affected or threatened. Preventive evacuations were also carried out in several localities, including El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira.

published.description: A wave of wildfires swept northern Algeria's forested provinces (including Constantine and Seraïdi) from mid-to-late July 2026 amid a severe regional heatwave, with GDACS tracking three concurrent Green-alert fire complexes that together burned roughly 39,400 hectares. Algeria's interior ministry confirmed six deaths and authorities reported over 100 people hospitalised and about 150 homes damaged in the Seraïdi area, with preventive evacuations also carried out in El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira; four people were arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting fires. As of 24-25 July 2026, GDACS records no further satellite thermal-anomaly detections for any of the three complexes, and Algerian civil protection authorities describe the blazes as under control.

impact.summary: GDACS's three concurrent Algeria wildfire complexes closed out at roughly 39,400 hectares burned in total: the Seraïdi/Constantine complex reached 11,942 hectares (about 1,210 people in the affected area, final thermal detection 25 July, alert level Green), a second complex 14,082 hectares (about 5,885 people affected, last detection 24 July) and a third 13,459 hectares (about 147 people affected, last detection 24 July). Algeria's interior ministry confirmed six deaths, and a 22 July Algerian Red Crescent/IFRC report via ReliefWeb put more than 100 people hospitalised and about 150 homes affected or threatened in Seraïdi, Annaba, with preventive evacuations in El Tarf, Béjaïa, Guelma and Bouira. No new thermal detections have been recorded since 24-25 July, and Algerian civil protection authorities describe the blazes as under control.

claims.text: The Flash Update on flash floods and landslides in Chattogram Division has been prepared by the Needs Assessment and Information Management Working Group and published on 09 July 2026, reporting 7 districts affected, 536,000 people affected, 11 deaths, 17,000 people temporarily displaced and 1,700 shelters activated.

Flash Update #2 (dated 11 July 2026, published 13 July) reports that 10 districts have been affected, more than 1.07 million people have been impacted, over 36,000 people remain temporarily displaced, and 26 casualties have been reported.

Situation Report #1 (dated 13 July 2026, published 14 July) reports 51 reported fatalities and more than 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts (Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Bandarban, Khagrachhari, Rangamati, Moulvibazar, Sunamganj, Habiganj, Sylhet and Cumilla), with more than 38,000 people staying in over 1,000 evacuation shelters as of 12 July, and significant damage to homes, water systems, roads, bridges and public infrastructure.

Oxfam situation report on the Bangladesh flash floods (15 July 2026): 1.11 million people affected across 10 districts, 53 fatalities and 39 injuries reported as of 15 July; Chattogram district was hardest-hit, with Chattogram city recording 412.3mm of rain in 24 hours, the highest single-day July rainfall in 42 years.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (14 July 2026): 1,074,534 people affected (NAWG figure) across 10 districts, about 38,500 people temporarily displaced (MoDMR figure) across 1,000+ shelters, 51 deaths, 267,918 households stranded, including 15 Rohingya refugee deaths reported by UNHCR among the Cox's Bazar camp toll.

BDRCS/IFRC nationwide situation report (posted 20 Jul 2026, originally published 19 Jul 2026): NAWG estimates 1,116,174 people affected across 10 districts (up from 1,074,534). MoDMR reports ~38,500 people temporarily displaced across 1,000+ shelters and 267,918 households stranded/isolated across seven districts (unchanged). At least 59 people have died nationwide (up from 53/51). In Cox's Bazar's 33 Rohingya refugee camps, flooding/landslides affected 28,000+ people, damaged 3,100+ shelters, and displaced 4,700+ individuals; UNHCR has confirmed 15 deaths among Rohingya refugees. As of 16 July only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (at Markuli, Sunamganj and Fenchuganj, Sylhet), and water levels in the Surma (Sylhet/Sunamganj) and the Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar rivers (Rangpur Division) were falling.

As of 16 July 9:00 AM, only the Kushiyara River remained above danger level (Markuli/Sunamganj and Fenchuganj/Sylhet stations); the Someshwari River at Kalmakanda had receded below danger level; Surma river conditions in Sylhet/Sunamganj were expected to improve within 24 hours; Teesta, Dharla and Dudhkumar river levels in Rangpur Division were falling and projected to fall further. BDRCS Emergency Operations Centre remains active.

Oxfam/CODEC Rapid Needs Assessment (RNA) Report on the Bangladesh Flash Flood 2026 (posted 21 Jul 2026): deep-dive assessment of Satkania and Banshkhali upazilas (Chattogram Division) found 360,000+ people affected in Satkania and 110,000+ in Banshkhali; 90-95% of surveyed households reported partial/complete loss of belongings; 92% of drinking water sources damaged/contaminated (94% in Banshkhali lacking safe water); all assessed latrines submerged; 90% of households reported insufficient food access and 59% reported signs of malnutrition.

UN Resident Coordinator's Office Bangladesh Situation Report #2 (dated 23 July 2026, data as of 22 July) reports approximately 1.28 million people affected across seven of the hardest-hit districts, 59 deaths, 74,479 houses damaged or destroyed, and about 436,000 people assessed as requiring humanitarian assistance; food, cash, health, protection, shelter and WASH assistance activities remain active, with continued risk flagged from forecast heavy rainfall in affected districts.

published.description: Monsoon-triggered flash floods and landslides have affected ten districts across Chattogram Division and adjoining south-eastern and north-eastern Bangladesh since early July 2026, with Chattogram city recording 412.3mm of rain in 24 hours — its highest single-day July rainfall in 42 years. Per the UN Resident Coordinator's Office Situation Report #2 (23 July 2026, data as of 22 July), about 1.28 million people are affected across the seven hardest-hit districts, 59 people have died nationwide (including 15 Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar camps, per UNHCR), 74,479 houses have been damaged or destroyed, and about 436,000 people need humanitarian assistance. Roughly 38,500 people were temporarily displaced across 1,000+ shelters and 267,918 households stranded, per the 19-20 July BDRCS/IFRC nationwide report. Food, cash, health, shelter, protection and WASH assistance remain active, and the event remains ongoing.

impact.summary: UN RCO Situation Report #2 (23 July 2026, data as of 22 July) records about 1.28 million people affected across the seven hardest-hit districts, 59 deaths nationwide (including 15 Rohingya refugees, per UNHCR), 74,479 houses damaged or destroyed, and about 436,000 people needing humanitarian assistance. claims.text: GDACS's forest-fire report for event 1030534 (Belgium) covers 14 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC to 17 Aug 2026 00:00 UTC, recording 6,356 hectares burned and 119 people within the affected/exposed population, with an overall alert level of 1.5 ('no humanitarian impact based on the burned area and the affected population and their vulnerability').

The European Commission's Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations service (17 August 2026, 'EU mobilises support as wildfires spread across Europe'): Belgium activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism; '2 planes' from the EU's rescEU firefighting fleet were dispatched from Sweden to Belgium, 'alongside 2 helicopters from the Netherlands, 2 from Norway and 2 from Germany,' supporting local firefighters battling the blaze in the Hautes Fagnes, where 'more than 3,000 hectares have burnt to date'; the Copernicus Emergency Management Service is active for wildfires in Belgium and several other European countries, providing rapid maps to help authorities organise their response.

published.description: Belgium's largest wildfire on record broke out on 14 August 2026 in the Hautes Fagnes (High Fens) nature reserve in eastern Belgium's Liege province, near the German border, during a prolonged drought and heat spell. GDACS recorded 6,356 hectares burned over 14-17 August with 119 people exposed, assessing an alert level of 1.5 -- a figure reflecting the reserve's sparse population rather than the fire's scale, which Belgian officials and international media described as the country's worst in a century. Belgium activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism: two rescEU firefighting planes were dispatched from Sweden alongside firefighting helicopters from the Netherlands, Norway and Germany, and the Copernicus Emergency Management Service was activated for rapid mapping, with more than 3,000 hectares burnt per the European Commission's 17 August statement. The fire prompted evacuation orders in Waimes and Butgenbach and threatened to cross into Germany near Monschau before rain and firefighting efforts halted its advance.

impact.summary: GDACS records 6,356 hectares burned in the High Fens (14-17 August 2026) with 119 people exposed and no confirmed deaths; the European Commission reported more than 3,000 hectares burnt in its 17 August statement as EU support mobilised. Belgium activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism, drawing two rescEU firefighting planes from Sweden and helicopters from the Netherlands, Norway and Germany, with Copernicus emergency mapping activated; no specific evacuation headcount has been published, though evacuation orders covered nearby towns.

published.description: Torrential rain from the remnants of Typhoon Maysak triggered severe flooding across Guangxi, Hunan, Hubei and neighbouring provinces of southern and central China in early-to-mid July 2026, pushing rivers and reservoirs past danger thresholds and submerging villages. GDACS assessed an overall Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact. A re-check of GDACS's event report on 1 August 2026 found the event record (GDACS ID FL 1103933) had continued to accrue episodes past the previously-recorded 7 July closure, with the reporting window now extending to 14 July 2026 and cumulative displacement revised sharply upward to 782,166 people (from an earlier 85,197); the confirmed death toll remains 12. No episode newer than 14 July exists, and with no activity for more than two weeks the event is assessed as concluded.

USGS's PAGER system assessed an Orange alert level, with approximately 10.5 million people exposed to Strong-to-Very-Strong (MMI VI+) shaking.

OCHA's Addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan -- Earthquake, Colombia (posted 20 August 2026, originally published 19 August 2026): "According to the most recent reports as of 17 August, 304 people had lost their lives and 4,400 had been injured... Damage to housing is extensive: 134,341 homes have been affected and 29,554 have been destroyed... 267 residential buildings collapsed... Search and rescue activities remain ongoing and have enabled the rescue of 338 people."

OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 008 (data as of 20 August 2026, 8 p.m. local time): the earthquake has affected more than 282,700 people and 153,300 households, resulting in 319 fatalities and the destruction of more than 31,400 homes. A State of Emergency remains in effect across 15 departments, and US$40 million has been mobilized to complement response and recovery efforts under the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) Addendum.

GDACS's earthquake report for this event (event id 1557236, episode 1724218) remains an Overall Red alert with a GDACS score of 2.2, now estimating about 5.4 million people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking, up from about 5.2 million previously recorded on the same page; the most recent listed activity is UNITAR-UNOSAT's 'Potentially Damaged Buildings' assessment, activated 21 August 2026 10:25 UTC.

The page's casualty line, citing media reports and not independently verified by GDACS, now reads 'at least 240 deaths' -- higher than, and not adopted in place of, the government-sourced UN News figure below.

Servicio Geológico Colombiano (10 August 2026): confirms the magnitude 7.4 event centered near San José del Palmar at a depth of about 103 km, recorded 18 aftershocks (magnitude 1.4-4.8) as of midday 10 August, describes it as 'the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in Colombia in the 21st century,' and notes more than 12,000 people from 900 populated centres reported feeling the earthquake. published.description: A magnitude 7.4 intermediate-depth earthquake struck western Colombia on 10 August 2026 at 12:34:28 UTC, centered 5 km south of San José del Palmar in Chocó Department at a depth of roughly 110 km; Colombia's geological survey described it as the seismic event of greatest magnitude recorded in the country in the 21st century. OCHA Colombia's Flash Update 008 (data as of 20 August) puts the toll at 319 deaths, with more than 282,700 people (153,300 households) affected across 15 departments and more than 31,400 homes destroyed; 4,400 injured and 426 missing remain the last-confirmed figures (Flash Update 007, 17 August), and search-and-rescue operations had saved 338 people as of that update. Both GDACS and USGS's PAGER system rate the event a Red alert for high humanitarian impact; GDACS now estimates about 5.4 million people within zones of MMI VII or greater shaking, up from an earlier 5.2 million. The government has activated emergency coordination centres in Bogotá, Quibdó, Armenia and Cali, and the international response continues to scale up.

claims.text: GDACS's Volcanic Eruption report for Fuego (Guatemala), updated 05 Aug 2026 08:09 UTC, gives the volcano's coordinates as 14.47°N, -90.88°W, rates the event overall alert level Green, and estimates approximately 1,480,000 people exposed within 30 km and 9,930,000 within 100 km, assessing that the eruption 'is unlikely to require external humanitarian assistance based on the exposed population and coping capacity.'

A Guatemalan Red Cross (Cruz Roja Guatemalteca) / IFRC situation report on ReliefWeb, published 4 August 2026, states that the Fuego eruption began at 08:30 local time on 3 August, that ash-and-gas columns reached 5,000-6,000 m above sea level dispersing more than 40 km to the west, that 9 seismic events generated pyroclastic density currents travelling 5-7 km down the Barranca Seca on the volcano's western flank (posing the greatest threat to communities in San Pedro Yepocapa, Chimaltenango), and that the Guatemalan government established a nationwide orange alert ('alerta anaranjada') to ready shelters and supplies, with CONRED issuing bulletins to authorities and the public.

A follow-up Guatemalan Red Cross / IFRC situation report on ReliefWeb, published 5 August 2026, states the eruption had continued atypically for more than 24 hours since its 3 August 08:30 start, with gas, lava and ash columns of 5,000-7,000 m and pyroclastic density currents of 5-7 km recurring in seven ravines (Seca, Taniluyá, Ceniza, Las Lajas, Honda, Trinidad and El Jute); per CONRED, at least 894 people were sheltered in 3 facilities in Sacatepéquez and Escuintla departments (most from Escuintla), more than 29,000 people were affected, and 'por el momento no se registran daños a personas y viviendas' (no injuries to people or damage to homes had been recorded at that time).

Re-checked 7 August 2026: GDACS's event report (eventid 1000145, updated 5 August 2026 08:09 UTC) still shows an overall Green alert with over 1,700 people evacuated and no deaths or injuries reported; no ReliefWeb or CONRED sitrep newer than the 5 August 2026 Guatemalan Red Cross/IFRC report (894 sheltered, 29,000+ affected, 0 deaths) has been found, though CONRED's 5 August 2026 bulletin ('Tras 50 horas de actividad, Volcan de Fuego retorna a sus parametros normales') indicates the paroxysmal phase has subsided.

OCHA's Latin America & the Caribbean Weekly Situation Update (7 August 2026) states: "Authorities evacuated 1,421 people to five shelters and reported that exposure to ashfall and volcanic hazards has affected more than 29,000 people across 18 communities, particularly Alotenango, the town closest to the volcano... as of 6 August, volcanic activity has begun to decrease from its peak intensity." No deaths are recorded.

published.description: A major paroxysmal eruption began at Volcán de Fuego, Guatemala's most active volcano, at 08:30 local time on 3 August 2026, sending gas-and-ash columns to 5,000-7,000 m above sea level and generating pyroclastic density currents that travelled 5-7 km down multiple ravines on the volcano's flanks. Guatemala's disaster coordination agency CONRED declared a nationwide orange alert and evacuated communities in Escuintla and Sacatepéquez departments as the eruption continued atypically for more than 24 hours. CONRED reported on 5 August 2026 that the volcano had returned to normal parameters after 50 hours of activity, and OCHA reported that volcanic activity had begun to decrease from its peak as of 6 August, with 1,421 people evacuated to five shelters and more than 29,000 people affected across 18 communities; no deaths have been recorded.

claims.text: UN News (5 June 2026), citing IOM: "nearly 1.5 million people without a stable place to live"; "more than 18,000 people" displaced in May 2026 alone from Cité Soleil attacks; the number of internally displaced people in Port-au-Prince rose "above 300,000" for the first time on record; "more than 110,000 Haitians" have been forcibly returned to the country since the beginning of 2026. IOM Chief of Mission Gregoire Goodstein: "Haiti's displacement crisis is entering an even more alarming phase."

Re-checked 12 August 2026: OCHA's 'Haiti: Nationwide Humanitarian Response (1-30 June 2026)' report (ReliefWeb, published 29 July 2026) confirms the 1.47 million/IOM Round 13 DTM figure (a 1 percent increase over Round 12) as the still-current national displacement total, including more than 300,000 in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area alone, and adds that a new wave of violence between 13-19 June forced over 5,000 additional people to flee Cite Soleil -- a component of, not a supersession of, the national total. UN News (6 August 2026) restates the BINUH figures already on file (613 killed, 375 injured, 176+ women and girls raped over 4.5 months through 31 July) without a newer nationwide aggregate.

UN News (6 August 2026): in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cite Soleil alone, at least 613 people were killed and 375 injured over a 4.5-month period through 31 July 2026, more than a third of them not associated with gangs (including 111 women and 77 children); over 18,000 people were displaced from those two neighbourhoods in the same period, and 176+ women and girls were reported raped by gang members, often as a form of punishment. The 13 June attack on a World Cup viewing crowd of about 300 people killed 61 and injured 20, including at least 7 children.

UN Security Council briefing (S/2026/574, 20 July 2026, per press.un.org): only 1,000 of the 5,550 authorized troops for the Gang Suppression Force have been deployed; the UN verified 2,088 grave violations against children in 2025. SRSG Carlos Ruiz Massieu reaffirmed that about 1.5 million people have been forced to flee their homes because of gang violence.

UN News (19 July 2026): "1.47 million people have fled their homes largely due to violence." During a Cité Soleil violence outbreak, "at least 542 people were killed and 355 injured," and "at least 176 women and girls were raped." Separately, at least 87 deaths have been reported from vigilante killings of suspected gang collaborators. "Around 6.4 million people need humanitarian assistance" and "more than 5.8 million people are expected to go hungry this year."

UN News (20 July 2026), 'LIVE: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future': reconfirms IOM's nearly-1.5-million displacement figure (originally reported 5 June 2026) as still current, reports on a UN Security Council discussion of the Gang Suppression Force, and notes that Haitian security forces have begun recording limited successes against armed gangs, pushing some criminal groups out of strategic locations in Port-au-Prince and reopening some major roads; the article provides no updated death-toll or displacement aggregate beyond the figures already reported. Re-checked 5 August 2026: no newer UN News, ReliefWeb, or OCHA report supersedes the 19-20 July 2026 figures (1.47M displaced, 542 killed in the Cité Soleil outbreak, 6.4M in humanitarian need, 5.8M facing hunger).

New localized report found 8 August 2026: a BINUH (UN Integrated Office in Haiti) report posted to ReliefWeb 6 August 2026 states that, in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area and Cite Soleil specifically, "between 6 March and 31 July 2026, at least 613 people were killed and 375 others injured, primarily during confrontations between criminal gangs... more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape" and "more than 18,000 people [were] forced to flee their homes" in that area; it also documents an attack after a 13 June FIFA World Cup match that killed at least 61 people. This is a more specific, localized casualty count for a sub-national area and period, and does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) or the broader 19 July UN News Cite Soleil figure (542 killed) already cited, which cover different scopes; no newer nationwide displacement aggregate has been published.

OCHA's Latin America & the Caribbean Weekly Situation Update (7 August 2026) reports that armed violence in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite department, displaced approximately 4,216 people on 28 July, with three displacement sites forced to close, triggering additional secondary displacement — a new localized incident that does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) already on file.

More than a third of the regional victims were not gang-affiliated, including 111 women and 77 children, and more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape, by gang members. The national displacement figure of nearly 1.5 million remains the latest confirmed IOM/DTM total found on ReliefWeb (originally reported 5 June 2026); no newer national total was located as of 10 August 2026.

published.description: Heavy monsoon rains since mid-July 2026 have driven concurrent flooding and landslides across five Indian states — Assam, Odisha, Gujarat, Kerala and Maharashtra — with Sphere India coordinating a multi-state humanitarian response. Combining the latest state figures gives a toll of at least 109 deaths and at least 347,155 people displaced or sheltering nationwide, and the event remains ongoing. Two small foreshocks preceded it, including a M4.1 on 14 July and a M4.7 88 minutes prior to the mainshock.

Approximately four million people experienced Moderate (MMI V) to Very Strong (MMI VII) shaking." PAGER's probabilistic fatality model places roughly 66% probability on the event causing between 1 and 100 fatalities, and about 27% probability of exceeding 100 fatalities. No revision to this page has occurred since 18 July 2026.

claims.text: WHO Representative to Sudan Dr. Shible Sahbani reported more than 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 confirmed deaths, a case fatality rate of 13.7 percent, in an outbreak affecting several states, mainly in the western part of the country, the Darfurs and the Kordofans, briefing journalists in Geneva on 10 July 2026. Aid officials say the true number of fatalities is likely much higher, and the disease is expected to spread further as the rainy season sets in, particularly among people who have fled towns and rural areas in North Kordofan.

ECDC's cholera worldwide monthly overview and its Weekly Communicable Disease Threats Report (Week 33, 8-14 Aug 2026) both confirm the Sudan cholera dataset has not been refreshed since a data cut of 12 July 2026: 1,511 cumulative cases and 153 deaths reported since 1 January 2026, ranking Sudan second globally after DRC (3,841 cases). WHO/EMRO's dedicated Sudan crisis page returned repeated server errors (HTTP 502) and could not be verified this session.

UN News report (14 July 2026), citing OCHA, reconfirms WHO's count of 1,330 confirmed cholera cases and 114 deaths as of 7 July 2026, and describes the outbreak's continued spread: new confirmed and suspected cases in Kalma/Kampala displacement camp (South Darfur) and Tawila (North Darfur); West Kordofan reporting the highest caseload with new suspected cases and deaths; and North Kordofan reporting 32 new suspected cases in Gharb Bara locality in a single day. WHO delivered 8.5 tonnes of medical supplies to Kadugli and Dilling, South Kordofan — its first shipment there since December 2024 — and UNICEF delivered health supplies to El Fula, West Kordofan, serving about 429,000 people.

WFP report (data as of 17 July 2026): regular power outages are disrupting water supplies in El Obeid, and more than 30 new cholera cases have been recorded there as the city's displacement and hunger crisis deepens.

UN Women statement (24 July 2026): 'Cholera is already spreading in Sudan, with 1,330 cases reported by WHO in early July,' confirming no revised national cumulative total has superseded the 7 July WHO count as of this date.

This multi-country surveillance figure is dated to 31 May 2026 and is superseded chronologically by the 1,330-case/114-death figure WHO's Representative to Sudan reported on 10 July 2026 for the same national outbreak; re-checked 5 August 2026, no WHO or ReliefWeb Sudan-specific update newer than the 10 July figure has been published, and no allowlisted source has declared the outbreak contained.

ECDC's cholera-monthly page (updated 27 July 2026) reports for Sudan: 'Since 11 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 502 new cases, including 153 new deaths' and, year-to-date, 'Since 1 January 2026 and as of 12 July 2026, 1 511 cases, including 153 deaths' — compared with 32,230 cases and 774 deaths in the equivalent 2025 timeframe (1 January-8 July 2025). The page also states a 58-year-old woman and her dog died on 8/14/2026 after driving into floodwaters near Yorktown.

The State of Indiana's own event announcement confirms that Governor Mike Braun declared a Statewide Disaster Emergency on Thursday, 13 August 2026, 'in response to widespread damage, power outages and flooding caused by this week's severe storms and derecho,' directing state agencies to coordinate emergency response across Franklin, Henry, Lake, LaPorte, Madison, Newton, Porter and Pulaski counties (Executive Order 26-21), and authorizing deployment of Indiana National Guard troops to Gary, Munster and Hobart for life-saving activities as well as cleanup and support.

published.description: Repeated rounds of severe thunderstorms and a derecho crossed Indiana between 11 and 17 August 2026, dropping over a foot of rain in places -- the heaviest totals, over 12 inches, east of Indianapolis -- and driving the White River to record levels. NWS Indianapolis recorded the river cresting at Anderson at 24.93 feet on 14 August, surpassing the all-time record of 23.60 feet set in 1913, and at Noblesville at 24.60 feet on 15 August, past that gauge's 1913 record of 23.80 feet; at Nora it reached 21.18 feet, its highest level since 1913. One death is confirmed: a 58-year-old woman and her dog died on 14 August after driving into floodwaters near Yorktown, though wider media reporting has described a higher statewide toll from the same storm system that no authoritative source has corroborated. Governor Mike Braun declared a Statewide Disaster Emergency on 13 August under Executive Order 26-21, covering eight counties from Franklin and Henry to Porter and Pulaski, and ordered Indiana National Guard troops to Gary, Munster and Hobart for life-saving work as well as cleanup and support; the storm sequence ended on 17 August and the response has moved to cleanup.

Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency on 10 August, with more than 16,000 acres burned and more than 6,000 people evacuated at that time, and FEMA authorized federal funds to assist Nevada in combating the Bug Fire. This followed Governor Ferguson's own statewide wildfire emergency proclamation of 1 August 2026. No casualty, structure-loss, or acreage figures are given in this release.

claims.text: On 7 August 2026 the US Department of Health and Human Services approved Governor Ferguson's request to declare a federal Public Health Emergency in response to the Eastern Washington wildfires, covering the same six counties (Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Yakima) and three tribal nations (Yakama Nation, Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, Spokane Tribe of Indians) already covered by the 4 August 2026 federal emergency declaration.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 7 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson's office announced that the US Department of Health and Human Services approved his request to declare a Public Health Emergency for the wildfire-affected areas of Eastern Washington -- Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties, plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians. This is a second, stacked federal declaration alongside the major disaster/emergency declaration Washington received on 4 August 2026. No death or displacement figures have been published on an allowlisted source.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Washington State
claims.text: On 10 August 2026, Governor Bob Ferguson signed an emergency proclamation suspending numerous state laws to help those affected by the wildfires, now covering Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens, Douglas and Yakima counties plus the Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation, the Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation, and the Spokane Tribe of Indians (adding Douglas County to the area covered by the 4 August federal emergency declaration). The Governor's office states: "My emergency proclamation waives and suspends numerous state laws so that help can move quickly," and the proclamation suspends disaster cash assistance eligibility requirements, personal document replacement fees, professional license renewal deadlines, unemployment benefit waiting periods and job-search requirements, a two-week limitation on eviction-related actions, healthcare provider licensing and supervision requirements, hospital and pharmacy licensing restrictions, and adult family home/assisted living facility capacity limitations, and waives late fees for employers unable to file or pay second-quarter 2026 taxes because of the wildfires. No death toll, injury count, acreage, containment, or displacement figures are given in this release.

published.description: Dozens of wildfires broke out across the Pacific Northwest in late July and early August 2026, burning hundreds of thousands of acres and forcing evacuations of tens of thousands of people across eastern Washington State and into Idaho. Governor Bob Ferguson proclaimed a statewide wildfire emergency on 1 August, and a federal emergency declaration approved on 4 August 2026 covers Chelan, Ferry, Okanogan, Spokane, Stevens and Yakima counties plus the Yakama Nation, the Colville Reservation and the Spokane Tribe of Indians; the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned statewide, the highest acreage since 2021, with 110 National Guard members activated. The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, had grown to 155,209 acres and was 53% contained as of 23 August 2026, with 1,563 personnel assigned and the northwest portion near Toats Coulee Road remaining active; full containment is estimated for 31 August. No confirmed death toll or structure-loss count has been published for the emergency as a whole.

impact.summary: The Sinlahekin Fire, the state's largest, started by a lightning strike on 26 July 2026 about 12 miles west of Tonasket and had grown to 155,209 acres at 53% containment as of 23 August 2026, with 1,563 personnel assigned; the northwest portion near Toats Coulee Road remained active toward Hodges Horse Pasture, with crews conducting contingency line work and an estimated full-containment date of 31 August. Statewide, the governor's office reports over 1,000 fires and approximately 425,000 acres burned, the highest acreage since 2021, with 200,000+ acres actively burning across 12 large fires at the emergency's height, 110 National Guard members activated and 13 State Fire Marshal task forces mobilized. Federal emergency and Public Health Emergency declarations cover six counties and three tribal nations; no confirmed death toll or structure-loss figure has been published.

claims.text: The Office of the Governor of West Virginia's own announcement states that on 21 July 2026, following severe storms producing flash flooding, landslides, road closures, damaging winds, torrential rainfall and mudslides across the state, Governor Patrick Morrisey declared a State of Emergency for all 55 West Virginia counties, effective for 30 days unless terminated earlier, with the most severe impacts concentrated in Lewis, Pleasants and Upshur counties.

published.description: Severe storms brought torrential rainfall to north-central West Virginia on 20-21 July 2026, triggering flash flooding, landslides, mudslides, damaging winds and road closures. Governor Patrick Morrisey declared a State of Emergency for all 55 West Virginia counties on 21 July 2026, with the most severe impacts concentrated in Lewis, Pleasants and Upshur counties. The governor's office reported approximately 85 rescues over a 20-hour span on 22 July, more than 3,100 Division of Highways employees and over 300 pieces of heavy equipment deployed, roughly 12,366 customers without power and three shelters open at Buckhannon, Weston and Philippi; by 24 July it recorded about 151 homes damaged in Upshur County and a National Guard deployment of 352 personnel and 84 vehicles, alongside over 1,700 registered volunteers. On 14 August 2026 the state extended the emergency through 19 September 2026 for twelve hard-hit counties -- Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pendleton, Pleasants, Randolph, Ritchie, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur and Wetzel -- so recovery operations and damage assessments can continue, while the declaration for the remaining 43 counties expires 20 August 2026.

impact.summary: The West Virginia governor's office reported approximately 85 water rescues over a 20-hour span on 22 July 2026, about 151 homes damaged in Upshur County, and a National Guard deployment that had grown to 352 personnel and 84 vehicles by 24 July, alongside more than 2,600 Division of Highways employees and over 1,700 registered volunteers. A State of Emergency covering all 55 counties was declared 21 July 2026 and later extended through 19 September 2026 for twelve of the hardest-hit counties, while the declaration for the remaining 43 counties expires 20 August 2026. No death or displacement figure has been confirmed by an authoritative source, though media reporting attributes two deaths in Upshur County to the flooding.

claims.text: On 25 June 2026 a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.

EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib conducted a field visit to La Guaira together with the UN Humanitarian Coordinator to review response efforts.

OCHA's Situation Report #24 (17 July 2026, 8:00 pm) states that, twenty-three days since the earthquakes, authorities report an official toll of 5,069 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,331 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report #26 (19 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 5,208 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,388 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes. An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months, on top of the US$632 million 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

Official toll: 5,346 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. The US$299 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan complements the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, increasing the target population from 5.5 million to 6.2 million people and raising total funding requirements from US$632 million to US$931 million.

Situation Report No. 30, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 23 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm. Authorities report 1,463 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. Starting with this edition, the report will be published on a weekly basis. The next edition will be released on 30 July.

OCHA Situation Report #31, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 31 July 2026, 5:00 pm: authorities report 1,500 aftershocks since the 24 June doublet earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). Official toll: 5,546 people dead and 16,740 injured; 17,907 people lost their homes. As of 30 July, 207,700 people (54% women and girls) have accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance. The additional US$299 million appeal remains in place, complementing the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan for combined requirements of US$931 million targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. The report continues to be published weekly.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: IOM's Earthquake Response Situation Report #19 (covering 31 July - 3 August 2026, published 4 August 2026) reports ongoing shelter and relief operations -- including 796 people from 221 households sheltering at the Jose Maria Vargas Sports Complex and cumulative distributions of 4,987 kitchen sets, 4,580 tarpaulins, 3,441 solar lamps, 3,313 water containers and 2,527 hygiene kits -- but does not include a death toll or injury figure. OCHA's 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' series remains at #31 (31 July 2026), with no #32 yet published; the official toll therefore remains unchanged at 5,546 dead and 16,740 injured.
The USGS is assessing earthquake-triggered landslide hazards generated by the 2026 Venezuela earthquake sequence.

International Medical Corps' Venezuela Earthquakes Situation Report #5 (published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: 'Official figures have confirmed 6,125 fatalities, 16,740 injuries and 17,907 people who have lost their homes' -- an increase in the confirmed death toll from the 5,546 recorded in OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026), while injury and homelessness figures are unchanged.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: OCHA's numbered 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' series has resumed and caught up to the higher toll -- Situation Report #32 (7 August 2026, 2:00 pm) states: "As of 03 August, authorities reported 6,125 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes. They also reported that 60,992 people received care at hospitals and 43,679 homes were evaluated, out of which 6,433 are at high risk... 16,51% of the total rubble has been cleared... nearly 212,000 people had access to essential services and humanitarian assistance," with 24,477 of 28,223 temporary-camp capacity occupied. This directly confirms, via OCHA's own series, the 6,125 death toll previously reported only by International Medical Corps; injuries (16,740) and people who lost their homes (17,907) are unchanged.

OCHA Situation Report #33 (14 August 2026, 14:00 local time): 'As of 10 August, authorities reported 6,301 deaths from the earthquakes,' 73,356 people received hospital care, 53,314 homes evaluated (9,567 at high risk), and about 23.26% of total rubble cleared; preliminary UNDRR estimates put direct damage to housing/infrastructure at approximately US$37 billion, while UNDP estimates direct physical damages at US$6.7 billion (6% of GDP); over 304,000 people (57% women and girls) had accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance as of 14 August, with the response scaling up to address 1.3 million people affected over the next six months.

As of 1 July 2026, nearly 2,000 deaths have been confirmed and more than 6,400 people rescued; 1.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance including 680,000 children across six affected states, with around 1,000 buildings and over 400 schools damaged and more than 600 aftershocks recorded since the initial quakes.

UN Daily Press Briefing (19 August 2026): "The death toll according to local authorities has surpassed 6,400" in Venezuela following the June earthquake doublet. No numbered OCHA 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' has been published since Situation Report #33 (14 August 2026); the weekly series' next edition is expected around 21 August.

OCHA's Situation Report #14 (07 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,685 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes. Authorities also reported that approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and that more than 1,076 aftershocks have been recorded, with at least seven (7) states impacted and La Guaira remaining the most affected state.

OCHA's Situation Report #15 (08 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,811 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and more than 1,100 aftershocks have been recorded. An additional appeal for US$296 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

A first assessment by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure at some $37 billion, comprising $24 billion in damage to buildings and another $13 billion in infrastructure; at least 79 transitional camps have opened in stadiums and sports centres, hosting displaced residents and providing aid.

OCHA's Situation Report #18 (11 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency; 1,171 aftershocks have been recorded, 17,907 people remain without housing, and 315 of those who died have yet to be identified. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan; an additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report No. 20 (13 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that, nineteen days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,561 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency, with more than 1,254 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed. The response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected populations, with a capacity of 25,064 people and a current occupancy of 20,231 people. A preliminary UNDP estimate indicates direct physical damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 percent of GDP, alongside the earlier UNDRR estimate of approximately US$37 billion. The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to US$200 million.

OCHA's Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

published.description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas, on 25 June 2026, forming a doublet with a magnitude 7.2 shock in the same sequence; at least seven states were impacted, with La Guaira the most affected. The UN Spokesperson's Office said on 19 August that the death toll "according to local authorities has surpassed 6,400"; the most recent numbered report, OCHA Situation Report #33 (14 August 2026), had put authorities' reported toll at 6,301 deaths as of 10 August, with 73,356 people treated at hospitals and 53,314 homes evaluated (9,567 at high risk); 16,740 injuries and 17,907 people who lost their homes remain the standing counts. Preliminary estimates put direct damage at some US$37 billion (UNDRR) and US$6.7 billion, about 6% of GDP (UNDP); a US$299 million addendum raised combined UN humanitarian requirements to US$931 million, targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected, over six months. The response remains in a scaled-up relief and early-recovery phase, with over 304,000 people (57% women and girls) having accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance as of 14 August.

Damage estimates stand at approximately US$37 billion (UNDRR, preliminary) and US$6.7 billion or about 6% of GDP (UNDP), against combined UN funding requirements of US$931 million targeting 1.3 million earthquake-affected people over six months. Over 304,000 people (57% women and girls) had accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance as of 14 August.

claims.text: OCHA's oPt Humanitarian Situation Report (23 July 2026) states: 'Fatalities linked to settler attacks in 2026 have already surpassed the total recorded during all of 2025, with 18 Palestinians killed as of 20 July compared with 17 throughout 2025,' and 'about 90 Palestinians were displaced by demolitions and settler attacks during the reporting period, most following a large-scale demolition carried out by Israeli authorities in a Bedouin community in Qalqiliya governorate.'

OCHA's oPt Humanitarian Situation Report (7 August 2026, reporting period 28 July-3 August) states: "During the reporting period, no Palestinian fatalities were reported in the West Bank. At least 37 Palestinians were injured by Israeli forces or Israeli settlers, and 35 settler attacks that resulted in casualties, property damage, or both were documented." This is a weekly update; it does not restate the cumulative 2026 totals (76 Palestinians and 3 Israelis killed) already on file, which remain unchanged.

OCHA oPt's Humanitarian Situation Report covering 28 July-3 August 2026 (published 6 August 2026) states that 'during the reporting period, no Palestinian fatalities were reported in the West Bank,' while at least 37 Palestinians were injured by Israeli forces or settlers and 35 settler attacks resulting in casualties and/or property damage were documented that week. A separate OCHA oPt report dated 31 July 2026 gives a cumulative 2026 toll of 76 Palestinians 'killed by Israeli forces or settlers or died of wounds sustained earlier' and approximately 2,300 people displaced since the start of 2026 due to settler attacks or access restrictions -- both broader-scope, cumulative figures that do not exactly match this record's existing deaths/displaced counts, so the recorded totals are retained pending reconciliation of scope.

UN Security Council briefing by Ramiz Alakbarov, Deputy Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process (11 August 2026): 'So far in 2026, 76 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank by Israeli forces or settlers, including 18 children. Three Israelis were killed in confrontations with Palestinians.' 'Some 3,800 Palestinians, nearly half of them children, were displaced due to settler violence, demolitions and evictions.'

OCHA oPt Humanitarian Situation Report (14 August 2026, covering 4-10 August): 38 incidents involving Israeli settlers resulted in Palestinian casualties and/or property damage; in Masafer Yatta, about 30 settlers attacked the Tuba community, injuring 5 and destroying 3 residential structures by fire (displacing 3 families, 23 people including 14 children); near Beit Furik/Beit Dajan, four attacks (6-8 August) injured 7 Palestinians; settlers attacked a Palestine Red Crescent Society team near Abu Njeim on 7 August, injuring 4 including 2 paramedics.

The same OCHA oPt report documents an Israeli forces operation in Qalandiya Camp injuring 51 Palestinians (44 physically assaulted including a 9-year-old, one hit by a rubber-coated metal bullet, six treated for tear gas inhalation) and demolishing 9 structures (displacing 13 households, 71 people including 31 children); West Bank-wide, 25 Palestinian-owned structures were demolished between 8-10 August, displacing 6 households (29 people, including 17 children).

Human Rights Watch (hosted on ReliefWeb): 'Two Israeli settler attacks on Tal village near Nablus in the West Bank on July 24, 2026, resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and two Israelis... The July 24 killings in Tal bring the Palestinian death toll in the occupied West Bank since July 19 to 10.' The incident triggered a wave of settler reprisal attacks on nearby Palestinian villages and the Israeli government's announcement of a 'major counterterrorism operation.'

UN Daily Press Briefing (21 August 2026): the Spokesperson's Office reported that, in an Israeli settler attack on a Palestinian community in Hebron, "a young Palestinian was shot and killed, another critically injured, and a home was set on fire," while other homes were damaged; Israeli forces said the shooting followed a stone-throwing incident by Palestinians that injured Israelis. The briefing also reported that three Palestinian families in Qusra village have remained confined to their homes for two weeks, surrounded by a heavy presence of Israeli forces and settlers, with Israeli forces present inside one of the three homes. It stated: "since the beginning of the year, 22 Palestinians have been killed in settler attacks: 12 by settlers, 7 by Israeli forces, and 3 where it remains unclear" -- up from the 18 reported as of 20 July.

Per the same ReliefWeb-hosted Human Rights Watch report: 'As of July 19, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported 68 Palestinians killed in the West Bank in 2026, at least 13 by settlers. OCHA reported that as of July 15, 20 Israelis had been injured in 2026 in the West Bank.'

Since Friday, eight Palestinians, including a boy, and two members of the Israeli military have also been killed in the region.' 'The number of settler attacks has increased each year since 2023... rising to 1,835 last year.' 'There were about 190 attacks per month in the first four months of 2026, putting the West Bank on a trajectory to reach more than 2,000 attacks by the end of the year.'
